fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled 512-byte msgpack input is unpacked; the resulting msgpack_object is a str8 string whose content is 126 control bytes 0x01, four ASCII 'A' bytes, the 4-byte UTF-8 sequence F4 8F BF BF (U+10FFFF) and two 'B' bytes. This object is the root converted to JSON.
MSGPACK_OBJECT_STR case forwards the raw string bytes (o->via.str.ptr, size 136) to the JSON string writer flb_utils_write_str, which escapes special characters.
Output budget available = left(767) - off(1 after the opening quote) = 766 bytes; this budget is the only bound used below.
First byte 0xF4 of the 4-byte UTF-8 sequence is negative as a signed char and casts to 0xFFFFFFF4 > 0xFFFF, so the c > 0xFFFF branch is taken; the escape is generated from the decoded codepoint.

Capacity check only verifies 6 free bytes, but the escape written below can be up to 8 bytes for codepoints > 0xFFFF (\u%04x renders up to 6 hex digits). With 760 bytes already written (126*6 escaped controls + 4 'A'), available - written == 6 passes the check.
codepoint 0x10FFFF formats to '\u10ffff', an 8-byte escape (2 backslash-u characters + 6 hex digits), longer than the 6 bytes the previous check allowed.

The 8-byte escape is copied to buf+1+760 .. buf+768; written becomes 768 and *off advances to 769, exceeding the 767-byte budget handed to this function. The 769-byte sds data area only covers indices 0..768.
With off == 769, this unconditional NUL write lands one byte past the 769-byte sds data area -> ASan heap-buffer-overflow (write of size 1).

via: root msgpack_object passed to msgpack2json STR case
encoded_to_buf copies len bytes to p

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: The description states that when encoding a message pack to JSON, a control character is escaped with a Unicode escape sequence, the code checks for 6 available bytes, but the escape can be longer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow when the escape is copied to the output buffer. In flb_utils_write_str the c > 0xFFFF branch (reached by the 4-byte UTF-8 sequence F4 8F BF BF = U+10FFFF inside the msgpack string) checks only 6 free bytes (line 687) yet produces the 8-byte escape '\u10ffff' (line 710); copying it (line 711) advances the write offset past the output budget and flb_msgpack_to_json's unconditional 'json_str[off] = 0' (line 656) then writes one byte past the heap allocation.
